title: Lighthouse Model Inspector — composite per-model & per-route dashboard
creator: Ava Patel
description: Design a unified per-model and per-route 'Lighthouse Model Inspector' in the Redwood Console that surfaces latency, throughput, token composition, KV cache efficiency, and cost signals in a single scrollable canvas. The goal is to give engineers and SREs a fast way to diagnose regressions, validate rollouts, and tie token economics to observed latency/throughput patterns. The inspector will be accessible from model pages and route pages and must support quick comparisons between model variants and rollback decision signals.
design_goals: Convey time-aligned relationships between throughput spikes and latency p50/p95/p99 shifts
Expose token composition per-request (prompt vs completion vs system vs assistant) via Token Waterfall visualization
Visualize cache effectiveness (KV cache hit rate) as an overlay band and allow filtering to cache-hit vs cache-miss traces
Surface cost signals (cost-per-token, cost-per-request) and show heatmap by time-of-day
Be lightweight and performant inside the Console (SVG/Canvas rendering, incremental updates) and accessible
Enable quick drilldowns into example traces, related PRs, and rollout configs
proposed_ui_components: Header: model/route selector, variant toggle, time-range picker, compare toggle
Top KPIs row: p50/p95/p99 latency, avg tokens/request, requests/s, estimated cost/hour
Composite time-series canvas (main): stacked throughput bars (requests/s) with overlaid latency lines (p50/p95/p99) and token-rate area
Token Waterfall small-multiples: median token composition, median completion length, error-highlight cases
Cache band: semi-transparent horizontal band under latency lines showing KV cache hit %, hover to show filtered traces
Cost heatmap strip: hourly cost intensity with quick jump-to-window actions
Event lane: annotations for deploys/rollouts, incidents, feature flags
Trace drawer: list of sampled requests in time window with play/pause streaming previews
CTA: create alert from current view and jump to rollback/rollout controls in Console
chart_spec_overview: The main canvas is a multi-layer time-series that aligns different signal types on common time bins (default 1m). Each layer has independent aggregation and sampling rules but uses the same time axis. Downsampling: use median for per-request token sizes, p50/p95/p99 for latency percentiles, sum for throughput. The Token Waterfall uses per-request stacked bar aggregation (median composition per bucket) and supports expand-to-sample. Cost heatmap is binned hourly with normalized color scale and min-max clamping.
chart_series_definitions: errors_rate: aggregation=sum, color=#DC2626, renderer=points with size by count, axis=left
interactions_and_behaviors: Hover crosshair: shows aligned tooltips for all series at exact timestamp with sample-count and bucket-aggregates
Brush-to-zoom: allows selecting a time window to zoom main canvas and populate Token Waterfall samples
Compare mode: overlay second model/route with configurable opacity and dashed stroke; differences can be toggled for each series
Annotation pins: click event lane pins to open related PR/incident (links to GitHub/Confluence)
Filter by cache-hit/miss: toggles to re-render latency lines for only cache-hit or cache-miss requests
Export sample traces: button to export selected samples to CSV or open in Trace Drawer
Create alert from selection: pre-fill alert rule with metric, threshold, window, and suggested notification channels
accessibility_considerations: Use color-blind safe palette and allow switching to high-contrast theme
All interactive elements reachable via keyboard; brush and zoom with arrow keys and +/-
Tooltips accessible via focus and provide full textual descriptions for screen readers
Provide data table fallback below canvas summarizing series for selected time window
Ensure aria-labels for chart controls, annotations, and compare toggle
